title: The Association Between Calretinin and the Function of Ganglion Cells in Hirschsprung Disease
brief_summary: This study aims to compare the outcomes of patients with long segment Hirschsprung disease or total colonic aganglionosis who had negative calretinin staining and positive ganglion cells on the proximal resection margins to those who had both positive findings.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Confirmed histopathological diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease from January 1, 1990 to August 31, 2019
* Long-segment Hirschsprung disease (type A and B)
* Total colonic aganglionosis (TCA)
* Surgery at CHUSJ
* Tissue blocks of proximal resection margin available for pathological analysis
* Minimum 1 month of postoperative follow-up

Exclusion Criteria:

* Short-segment Hirschsprung disease (conventional form, rectosigmoid junction)
* Total colonic with small bowel aganglionosis (TCSA)
* Surgery done at another institution
* Early deaths
* Lost to follow-up
* No documented post-operative outcome
study_population: Patients with Hirschsprung disease and a transition zone more proximal to the distal sigmoid
